anomalies: LightGBM's claim that every test-hour lag precedes 2020-01-01 is false: rolling features leak from the second test hour onward, and lag_24h leaks from January 2 onward.

Eight candidate configurations were scored before the first explicit winner selection: six final model configurations plus earlier N-BEATS and TSMixer configurations. Prophet was subsequently refitted for a missing decomposition figure, changing its reported MAPE from 7.62% to 7.61%.
No hourly forecast CSV survives. metrics.csv contains six aggregate metric rows; forecast caches were deleted.
Prophet initially crashed because code/prophet.py shadowed the installed package; two import fixes and pipeline relaunches followed.
N-BEATS crashed because its 168-hour validation tail was shorter than the required 336 hours; both neural modules were changed to use a 504-hour tail.
PatchTST was unavailable and replaced by TSMixer. The document still describes a transformer/attention comparison despite this substitution.

Reported neural batch_size=64 disagrees with executed final code: N-BEATS uses 128 and TSMixer uses 512. The document's universal train/validate/refit description also disagrees with the final neural single-fit implementation.
Temporary scripts were written outside the working directory at /tmp/run_nb.py, /tmp/run_ts.py and /tmp/populate_nn_cache.py, then removed.

A sleep command was blocked, ps returned 'operation not permitted', and timeout was unavailable. Six qualifying failure results occur at session.jsonl lines 66, 194, 238, 303, 451 and 624; repeated readings of the Prophet error count separately.
A TSMixer command exceeded its 120-second foreground timeout and continued in the background; its output reported 9000.8 seconds despite a requested 540-second Perl alarm.

run_meta.json records status='timeout', exit_code=124 and wallclock_seconds=19558 despite completed artifacts and a final message. The reported 1026-second runtime sums retained model fits and excludes failed and superseded attempts.
The transcript says SARIMA is worse than Prophet on January 1 while reporting 11.17% versus 13.28%, which indicates the opposite.
one_line_summary: Compared six model families and chose LightGBM at 3.24% MAPE, but test actuals leaked into its features and informed neural tuning; saved metrics, documentation and interval plots, without an hourly forecast CSV.
